preamble: Note added 8 September 2011. There is a spelling mistake, involving one P too many, in the solution to 9 across.

clue.text: SHIFT jams — almost hit OK + CANCEL for dead icon …

indicators.note: shift, written like a keyboard key, tells us to move these letters around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word hit loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a computer keyboard is hammering SHIFT, OK and CANCEL as the machine jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts hit to HI; JAMS, HI, OK and CANCEL are then shuffled together. The keyboard picture hides a tribute to a pop star who had recently died.
explanation.definitionFit: The King of Pop died in 2009, so he is an icon who is no longer alive.

clue.text: Picking up fun guy that could make your head spin?

definitions.text: Picking up fun guy that could make your head spin?

parts.words: Picking up fun guy that could make your head spin?
parts.note: fun guy sounds like fungi, and picking hallucinogenic fungi could make your head spin

explanation.surface: Someone at a party picks up an entertaining man who could turn their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking up' seems to be about flirting, but it means collecting from a field; 'fun guy' said aloud sounds like fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallucinogenic mushrooms containing psilocybin cause altered perception, making your head spin.

clue.text: Head for lavatory — is tension breaking into location of hadron collider?

indicators.note: breaking into means the letters go inside the laboratory's name

parts.note: the Large Hadron Collider is at CERN, near Geneva
T is the symbol for tension in physics

explanation.surface: Someone heading for the toilet wonders whether tension is breaking out at the particle physics lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is not a direction but the sailor's word for a toilet; IS and T go into CERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is the water tank that flushes a toilet, a key part of the lavatory or head.

clue.text: Philosopher unconventional to realist

indicators.note: unconventional means arranged in an unusual way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A philosopher is described as unconventional compared with a realist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges the letters of 'to realist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was an ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander the Great.

clue.text: This stops kissers getting chaps lap dancing with Elvis

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the words lap and Elvis are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men at a club watch a lap dancer performing with an Elvis impersonator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges LAP and ELVIS together. 'kissers' is slang for lips, and 'chaps' are not men but cracks in dry skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm put on the lips protects them from chapping, so it stops chapped lips.

clue.text: Ford's early model passed by German manufacturer's checks

indicators.note: passed by means the letter is overtaken on both sides, ending up inside the carmaker's name

parts.note: Audi is a German carmaker; with the possessive it gives Audi's
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: An old Ford car is overtaken on the road by a German-made vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside AUDI'S, between the I and the S. The car-chase picture hides a word for inspections of accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Audits are official inspections of accounts, so they are checks.

clue.text: Two kings turn to pawns for weapons producer

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
R, for rex, is Latin for king
a U-turn turns you round, so turn gives U
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A chess move: two kings turn into pawns, as if from a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Krupp was the German steel and armaments firm. The chess picture hides that the two kings are two different letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Krupp was a German industrial company famed for producing artillery and armaments.

clue.text: Singer has straight daughter — alternatively the opposite?

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
the opposite of straight, meaning heterosexual, is bi
the opposite of daughter is son

explanation.surface: A singer has a heterosexual daughter, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opposite' applies to both straight and daughter, giving BI and SON. Roy Orbison was an American singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Orbison was an American singer famous for songs like Oh, Pretty Woman.

clue.text: To insert Always, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words might be arranged another way, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A question about how to use a well-known brand of feminine hygiene product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'To insert Always'. Always is a brand of the product, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Always is a brand of these pads, which are inserted into underwear, giving an example.

clue.text: … spread story: icon covering head in shocking Pepsi outburst

indicators.note: covering means the idol word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: an icon, an idol worshipped by fans, can be called a god

indicators.note: head in tells us to take the first letter of shocking
outburst says the letters of Pepsi burst out into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity's hair caught fire while filming a Pepsi advert, and the shocking story spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head in' takes S from 'shocking' and 'outburst' rearranges the drink's name. The grid's spelling has a P too many, as the puzzle's own note admits; the usual spelling has one P.
explanation.definitionFit: To gossip is to pass on rumours, so to have gossiped is to have spread a story.

clue.text: There's no light here — Man United's backing supporter …

indicators.note: backing means the club's initials are read backwards

parts.note: MU is the short form of Manchester United, the football club
a bra supports the bust, so it is a supporter

explanation.surface: A Manchester United fan stands in the dark, cheering on the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns MU into UM; 'supporter' seems to be a football fan but is a piece of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, where all the light is blocked.

clue.text: … one supports this in United's home?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the city name, so the letters around it are taken away

parts.note: Manchester United play in the city of Manchester

explanation.surface: Following on from the last clue, a fan wonders what the football club's home ground holds up.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside MANCHESTER once MAN and ER are taken away. 'one' refers back to the supporter (a bra) in the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is worn to support the bust, which sits on the upper body or torso.

clue.text: A new suggestion for wager — Ascot, firm going, Dettori finally getting his starting orders?

parts.note: a tip is a tipster's suggestion of what to bet on

indicators.note: going means the firm's letters leave the racecourse name

parts.note: CO, short for company, is a firm

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Dettori

explanation.surface: A racing tip: at Ascot, on firm going, the jockey Frankie Dettori gets his instructions before the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' takes CO out of ASCOT to leave AST. 'going' and 'starting orders' look like racing words; Ascot is an English racecourse and Dettori a famous jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters, the dishes ordered to begin a meal.

clue.text: Foreign news breaking: "Union backing musical"

indicators.note: breaking means the letter splits the other letters open
backing means the musical's title is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron
news read as new plus new: N twice, N being the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline reports that a trade union is putting money into a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as two lots of new, NN. 'backing' turns the musical's name round, and 'breaking' puts the pair inside. The surface reads like a headline about a union funding a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not native to a place has come from elsewhere, so it is alien or not local.

clue.text: See 17
Protector of plant's opening job for warder

definitions.meaning: in botany, a pair of these cells surrounds each stoma, the pore in a leaf, and controls it
a prison warder's task is to watch over a prisoner's room

explanation.definitionFit: Botanists name the cells flanking a leaf pore this way; read literally it is guarding a prison room.

clue.text: Set to grow weed in this?

definitions.text: Set to grow weed in this?

parts.note: to plant something is to set it in soil to grow
pot and weed are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A gardener asks where to put a seedling, or someone wonders where to grow cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a container for planting something, which could be cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A container of soil is where you would set a plant, including weed, to grow.

clue.text: Ulterior motive of Häagen-Dazs?

parts.note: the ice-cream brand name has a word for a list of business to discuss tucked inside its letters, across the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the real reason behind the ice-cream brand might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: in hAAGEN-DAzs the letters AGENDA can be found, so the brand has an agenda concealed within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret purpose kept from others is a concealed plan, so it is an ulterior motive.

clue.text: Bed for 20 — he needed it to check out university?

parts.words: he needed it to check out
parts.note: in darts a player must finish, or check out, on a double, so the darts player at 20 needed one

explanation.surface: A darts player needs a double twenty to finish the game, then leaves for university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed for 20' looks like the double-20 bed on a dartboard, but it is the letter W, which sits at the bottom of BRISTOW (20-down).
explanation.definitionFit: The letter W is named this way, and W is the last letter, the base, of the darts player's name.

clue.text: He helps priest change, we hear, by holding ring

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for change is said aloud and gives a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to alter something is to change it

indicators.note: holding means the word by wraps around the ring letter

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A helper assists a priest getting changed, standing by and holding a ring at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' swaps the word for change for one that sounds the same, a church table. 'change' looks like the priest getting dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy who serves a priest at the altar during church services is his assistant.

clue.text: "Bullseye … regains it" — Sid Waddell initially going over to darts player

indicators.note: going over means the last two initials go around the word to
initially tells us to take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A darts commentator, Sid Waddell, describes a player regaining the bullseye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B, R, I, S, W, and S and W go over TO. Sid Waddell was the BBC voice of darts; Eric Bristow was a world champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Bristow was a five-time world darts champion, nicknamed the Crafty Cockney.

clue.text: Good to go over writing material for "Chinese Tree"

indicators.note: over means the other letters go around the writing material

parts.note: taken from the phrase to go, giving the verb
ink is a material used for writing

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to go over their writing about a Chinese tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good to go' looks like one phrase meaning ready, but it splits into G and GO, which wrap around the writing material.
explanation.definitionFit: The ginkgo or maidenhair tree is native to China and grown worldwide.

clue.text: Shell and scramble evolutional egg time

indicators.note: scramble, as you would with eggs, tells us to mix the remaining letters up
to shell is to strip off the outside, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: shell some eggs and scramble them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' strips E and L from EVOLUTIONAL to leave VOLUTIONA, and 'scramble' rearranges those letters. 'Shell', 'scramble' and 'egg' all suggest cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation is when an ovary releases an egg, so it is the time for eggs.

clue.text: In the style of Calvin Klein — sadly no longer in use

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
CK is the brand initials of the fashion designer Calvin Klein

explanation.surface: Clothing in a fashion designer's style has sadly gone out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: ALA (à la) plus CK. The fashion surface hides an old-fashioned exclamation of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic cry of grief meaning alas, so it is an obsolete way to say sadly.

clue.text: OK I admit partially backing Japanese drum

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly admits they are partly in favour of a Japanese drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' points to the letters OKIAD within 'OK I admit', and 'backing' reads them backwards. 'backing' looks like support for the drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Daiko is a Japanese word for a large drum, also used for taiko drumming.

clue.text: Spice girl with a soprano

parts.note: Mel B was one of the Spice Girls pop group

explanation.surface: A member of the Spice Girls teams up with an opera singer.
explanation.walkthrough: MEL B was Scary Spice in the British girl group the Spice Girls. Nellie Melba was a famous Australian soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Nellie Melba was a celebrated Australian operatic soprano, giving her name to peach melba.

clue.text: 70s' clothing sounds like Noddy Holder's cup of tea

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the phrase is said aloud in that accent

parts.note: Noddy Holder, singer with the 1970s band Slade, has a strong Black Country accent, in which a cuppa tea comes out differently

explanation.surface: A 1970s pop star's favourite drink sounds like an item of clothing from that decade.
explanation.walkthrough: In a West Midlands accent like Noddy Holder's, 'cuppa tea' is said with vowels close to this tie. Slade were a 1970s glam rock band, so the clothing fits the era.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipper ties, very wide and often loudly patterned neckties, were a fashion item of the 1970s.

clue.text: Without a run rate, almost leg before wicket, is possible match decider

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, no runs
to rate is to value, as worth means value

indicators.note: almost means the word leg loses its last letter

parts.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: a batsman's poor run rate and a near leg-before-wicket decision may decide the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts leg to LE. The method is the cricket rule for setting a revised target when weather shortens a one-day match; leg before wicket (lbw) is a way to be out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duckworth-Lewis method calculates the winning target in rain-shortened one-day cricket, so it can decide results.
